headline: Users Express Fear That Their Thoughts 'Have a Comment Section'
subheadline: Anxiety that inner monologue is being observed and judged by unknown viewers
summary: A new form of existential paranoia involves the fear that one's private thoughts have an audience leaving reactions.
content:
A Threadit thread asking "Does anyone else worry their thoughts have a comment section?" has revealed a widespread and deeply unsettling form of modern anxiety.

The original post, by u/PrivatePublic, explains: "Sometimes I'll have a thought—just a normal thought—and I get this feeling like... someone is reading it. And judging it. And maybe downvoting it. Like my brain has a comment section I can't see."

The post received 8,000 responses expressing similar fears. Users describe feeling "observed" during private moments, sensing "engagement metrics" on their thoughts, and experiencing what one called "the phantom notification of internal criticism."

"I had an embarrassing thought last week," wrote one commenter. "Immediately felt like someone left a comment saying 'cringe.' But it was just me. In my head. Alone. I think."

The phenomenon appears connected to social media saturation. Users accustomed to having every public statement rated and responded to have internalized that framework for private cognition.

"I caught myself mentally defending a thought I hadn't shared with anyone," reported another user. "Like I was preemptively responding to criticism that didn't exist. But what if it does exist? What if someone is leaving comments on my thoughts and I just can't see them?"

Psychologists acknowledge the phenomenon is concerning. "The boundary between public and private has eroded," explained Dr. Patricia Huang. "We've trained ourselves to anticipate judgment on everything we express. It makes sense that some people would extend that anticipation to things they haven't expressed yet."

One commenter offered an even more disturbing perspective: "What if the thoughts you decide not to post... still get seen? What if everything is being commented on, always?"

The thread has 847 upvotes. The top comment reads: "I was going to type something but now I'm too self-conscious."

Second comment: "See? It's already happening."
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
